To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
IL‐6, eotaxine, IL‐12p70, IL‐8 and MCP‐1 are suitable biomarkers for the diagnosis of IAI after orthopaedic implant surgery, while IL‐1ra can be used for prognostic purposes.
the serum cytokine profiling may be a useful tool for early diagnosis of IAI after orthopaedic surgeries.
the serum cytokine profiling can be used as a diagnostic marker of implant associated infections after orthopedic surgery.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of candidate cytokines for IAI diagnosis after orthopaedic implantation.
the use of cytokine profiling for the diagnosis of implant‐related infections.
the development of a multiplex assay using serum cytokine profiling to detect IAI in the future.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cytokines IL‐6, and IL‐12 are suitable biomarkers to be used for IAI diagnosis, while the cytokines IL­‐1ra and, IL‐8 can be used as prognoses.
the cytokine profile of IL‐1ra (pre‐OP), IL‐6 (pre‐OP, COI, and post‐OP), IL8 (pre‐OP and post‐OP) and IL12 (COI) may be useful for diagnosis of IIA after orthopaedic procedures.
the use of CRP alone for IAI diagnosis is insufficient.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the serum cytokine profiling is suitable for early diagnosis of IAI after orthopaedic implant surgery.
CRP is not a reliable marker for IAI, and that IL‐6, IP‐10 and IL‐12 are suitable biomarkers for IAI diagnosis.
IL‐6, IP‐10 as well as IL ‐8 may be used for early diagnosis of IAI after orthopaedic procedures, whereas IL‐1ra may be used as a prognostic marker prior to surgery.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cytokine profiles can be used for diagnosis of ICI.
serum cytokine profiling is a suitable approach to identify candidate biomarker(s) for IAI.
cytokines are more reliable than CRP for the diagnosis of IAI.
